StellarEvolutionTracks — SampleOutputs Guide

Version: 1.8.0; Build: a33f673a91a1; Date: 2026-09-27.

These figures and selected console values accompany the Extended-style and Short-style Beats Help files. Run each command from the program folder; the command writes an image to ./figures. Numerical values below are taken from the same run that produced its image.

Beat 0: The Sun is not a constant

Command: python main.py --mode tracks --mass 1.0 --no_postms --outdir ./figures --dpi 150

The solar-mass main-sequence track and its changing luminosity and temperature.

What it shows

  • The luminosity changes even while hydrogen burns in the core.
  • The zero-age and terminal-age points bound the main-sequence track.
  • The plotted temperature is an effective surface temperature, not a core temperature.

Headline values

  • ZAMS: 0.72 L☉, 0.89 R☉, and 5636 K.
  • TAMS: 2.198 L☉ and 5716 K.
  • Main-sequence lifetime: 9.73 Gyr.
  • Helium core at TAMS: 0.1123 M☉.

Beat 1: Mass sets the main-sequence lifetime

Command: python main.py --mode hr --masses 1,2,5,10 --no_postms --outdir ./figures --dpi 150

Four main-sequence tracks compared at distinct initial stellar masses.

What it shows

  • More massive tracks occupy hotter and brighter regions of the HR diagram.
  • The mass-dependent end of core hydrogen burning is visible on each track.
  • The figure uses the same composition and closures for all four masses.

Headline values

  • Main-sequence lifetime at 1 M☉: 9.73 Gyr.
  • At 2 M☉: 1.361 Gyr.
  • At 5 M☉: 0.1685 Gyr.
  • At 10 M☉: 0.03469 Gyr.

Beat 2: Three closures a one-zone model cannot derive

Command: python main.py --mode tracks --mass 1.0 --no_postms --core_weight 1 --outdir ./figures --dpi 150

The solar-mass track with core weighting raised to unity.

What it shows

  • The larger core weighting changes the pace and direction of the solar-mass track.
  • The imposed closure affects the luminosity and the lifetime together.
  • Compare directly with Beat 0 at the default core weight of 0.360.

Headline values

  • Core weight: 1.000 (default reference: 0.360).
  • TAMS: 15.99 L☉ and 9388 K.
  • Main-sequence lifetime: 5.476 Gyr.
  • Beat 0 reference: 2.198 L☉, 5716 K, and 9.73 Gyr.

Beat 3: Leaving the main sequence

Command: python main.py --mode tracks --mass 5.0 --outdir ./figures --dpi 150

A five-solar-mass track including its schematic post-main-sequence crossing.

What it shows

  • After hydrogen exhaustion, the schematic Hertzsprung-gap prescription continues the track.
  • The bright post-main-sequence segment is much shorter lived than core hydrogen burning.
  • The endpoint marks helium ignition in this toy prescription.

Headline values

  • ZAMS: 284.6 L☉, 2.227 R☉, and 15,885 K.
  • Main-sequence lifetime: 0.1685 Gyr.
  • Schematic post-main-sequence duration: 0.0002388 Gyr.
  • Endpoint: 868.94 L☉, core mass 0.7689 M☉, age 0.1687 Gyr.

Beat 4: A cluster on one diagram

Command: python main.py --mode hr --masses 0.6,0.8,1.0,1.2,1.5,2.0,3.0,5.0,8.0 --isochrones 0.1,1,5,10 --t_max 60 --outdir ./figures --dpi 150

An HR diagram of nine tracks and four cluster-age isochrones.

What it shows

  • Isochrones connect equal-age locations on separate tracks.
  • The main-sequence turn-off shifts toward lower masses at later ages.
  • The high-mass post-main-sequence segments are schematic, not an evolutionary survey.

Headline values

  • Nine initial masses: 0.6 to 8.0 M☉.
  • Four isochrone ages: 0.1, 1, 5, and 10 Gyr.
  • Turn-off masses at those ages: 6.285, 2.289, 1.252, and 0.991 M☉.
  • Main-sequence lifetimes: 45.05 Gyr at 0.6 M☉ and 0.05769 Gyr at 8 M☉.

Beat 5: Where the track stops

Command: python main.py --mode tracks --mass 0.6 --t_max 200 --outdir ./figures --dpi 150

The endpoint of a low-mass track on the schematic degenerate giant branch.

What it shows

  • The lower-mass star leaves the main sequence after a long hydrogen-burning phase.
  • Its modeled post-main-sequence branch reaches the imposed low-mass endpoint.
  • The handoff to a helium-white-dwarf remnant is a heuristic, not a self-consistent single-star history.

Headline values

  • Initial mass: 0.6 M☉.
  • Main-sequence lifetime: 45.05 Gyr.
  • Post-main-sequence duration: 14.11 Gyr; total age 59.15 Gyr.
  • Endpoint helium-core mass: 0.4200 M☉.

Beat 6: A star the size of the Earth

Command: python main.py --mode wdcool --wd_mass 0.6 --outdir ./figures --dpi 150

The mass–radius and cooling panels for a 0.6-solar-mass white dwarf.

What it shows

  • The upper-left panel relates white-dwarf mass and radius.
  • The remaining panels show core temperature, luminosity, and cooling age.
  • The Chandrasekhar boundary is shown for this fixed composition.

Headline values

  • Mass: 0.6000 M☉; radius: 8840.9 km (1.388 Earth radii).
  • Central density: 3.2070 × 10⁹ kg/m³.
  • Core temperature: 3.000 × 10⁷ K to 3.000 × 10⁶ K.
  • Cooling age: 5.6235 Gyr, both RK4 and exact.

Beat 7: A white dwarf fades

Command: python main.py --mode wdcool --wd_mass 1.0 --outdir ./figures --dpi 150

The corresponding panels for a 1.0-solar-mass white dwarf.

What it shows

  • The more massive white dwarf has a smaller modeled radius.
  • Its luminosity falls as its core cools.
  • At fixed envelope parameters and the same temperature endpoints, the simple cooling age is unchanged.

Headline values

  • Mass: 1.0000 M☉; radius: 5716.5 km (0.897 Earth radii).
  • Central density: 2.8284 × 10¹⁰ kg/m³.
  • Luminosity: 9.8633 × 10⁻² to 3.1190 × 10⁻⁵ L☉.
  • Cooling age: 5.6235 Gyr for the same temperature interval.

Beat 8: An ideal neutron gas

Command: python main.py --mode nsmr --eos neutron --outdir ./figures --dpi 150

A general-relativistic sequence of ideal degenerate neutron-gas stars.

What it shows

  • The central turning point is an interior maximum of the relativistic sampled sequence.
  • The stable branch and the higher-density branch are drawn separately.
  • The ideal gas falls below the roughly two-solar-mass observational benchmark.

Headline values

  • Maximum sampled mass: 0.7100 M☉ at radius 9.313 km.
  • Central density there: 3.3304 × 10¹⁸ kg/m³.
  • Compactness there: GM/Rc² = 0.1126.
  • Peak sound-speed ratio on the stable branch: 0.3653 c.

Beat 9: How stiff must nuclear matter be?

Command: python main.py --mode nsmr --outdir ./figures --dpi 150

A general-relativistic sequence for the stiff toy polytrope.

What it shows

  • The repulsion surrogate produces a higher maximum mass than the ideal neutron gas.
  • The mass–radius star and central-density panel mark the same sampled maximum.
  • The reported cutoff check tests radius sensitivity at the maximum-mass model.

Headline values

  • Maximum sampled mass: 2.1754 M☉ at radius 11.692 km.
  • Central density there: 1.5013 × 10¹⁸ kg/m³.
  • Compactness there: GM/Rc² = 0.2747.
  • Peak sound-speed ratio: 0.8364 c; surface-radius drift at the peak: 0.000% on tightening the 10⁻¹⁴ cutoff.

Beat 10: Newton versus Einstein

Command: python main.py --mode nsmr --eos neutron --newtonian --outdir ./figures --dpi 150

A Newtonian sequence of ideal degenerate neutron-gas stars.

What it shows

  • The Newtonian sampled mass continues to rise through the plotted grid.
  • No relativistic turning-point stability or gravitational redshift is assigned.
  • The compactness diagnostic exposes where a Newtonian treatment is unphysical.

Headline values

  • Largest sampled mass: 3.5423 M☉ at radius 6.950 km (no maximum established).
  • Central density there: 5.0000 × 10¹⁹ kg/m³.
  • Compactness there: GM/Rc² = 0.7526, a Newtonian diagnostic only.
  • Six of 40 sampled radii lie within their own Schwarzschild radii; redshift is withheld.

Notes for evaluation

The figures are teaching-model outputs with prescribed closures and simplified equations of state. The polytrope is a stiffness illustration; the Newtonian high-compactness points do not describe realizable neutron stars. Read the two tutorial formats for exercises and interpretations. Images are embedded so the guide remains usable without external figure files.

Image provenance: All eleven PNG figures above were regenerated with the displayed commands from StellarEvolutionTracks 1.8.0, build a33f673a91a1, on 2026-09-27, using Matplotlib at 150 dpi. Console values were recorded from these same runs.
